articleSummary: An international study tests 18 molecules derived from known antimalarials, including pironaridine and quinacrine, against malaria parasites. articleSummary: Tetrabutylammonium (TBA), isolated from Anthopleura cascaia sea anemone venom from São Sebastião, Brazil, shows activity against multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. In antibacterial-activity-guided work, a disc-diffusion halo led to HPLC fractionation and microdilution, with mass spectrometry confirming TBA as the active compound; synthetic TBA retained activity. Among several resistant K. pneumoniae clinical isolates, TBA produced variable growth inhibition, with the three most susceptible isolates showing strong biocidal effects where treatment options were exhausted. In silico analyses suggest efflux-pump inhibition as a potential mechanism. The study also tested MDR Acinetobacter baumannii and Escherichia coli, but activity was clearest for K. pneumoniae. TBA exhibited low predicted toxicity, supporting its potential as a novel therapeutic option for MDR K. pneumoniae infections when conventional antibiotics fail.

The initiative represents a significant step toward reducing arboviral transmission in Anápolis and could serve as a model for broader public health efforts.

articleHeadline: In Russia, the spread of the drug-resistant tuberculosis strain EurA1.1 has been detected.
articleSummary: Irish researchers conducted genomic analysis of EurA1.1, a drug-resistant lineage of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, assessing 1,362 genomes, including 62 isolates from Russia. The work, published in npj Antimicrobials and Resistance, highlights the ongoing regional threat of resistant TB in Europe and Russia.
